title: LENS: the public API surface as a whole
summary: The surface's mechanics are the best part of the kernel and beat every period peer on an 8088. Packages make direct far calls into a fixed table, with no relocation and no loader fixups. Cells come in three shapes chosen by how often they are called, and the inline cell was measured at 52-57 cycles against 159-162 for a SLOT. Callbacks are plain near procs because the kernel loads DS from W_SEG, which Win16 needed MakeProcInstance for. The binary decode gate (t_api_abi) and the fingerprint lock (abilock) make collisions and silent contract changes fail `make`. What lags is the model around the mechanics. A package cannot learn at runtime which cells the kernel has, so a new package on an old kernel with the same PKG_FMT still calls past the end of the table. The only common refusal signal is CF; what AX means is up to each cell's author. Rules about which task or context may call a cell are prose with almost no enforcement. The surface has grown by accretion: ten handler setters and seven flag setters, verbs in AL, AH or BL depending on the door, and three meanings each of CLIP, FS and DESK. Two contract bugs are live. OSAPI_RAND's low bits repeat with a short period and six games read them. kern_small's OSAPI_FS_OP overwrites AX although the SDK says every register is kept. The ABI gate decodes one kernel out of four. The flag-day list already covers the byte savings. What is new here is about the model: a major/minor version pair (the table end is published in a free word at no byte cost), one refusal code, and a window class record kept in the package in place of per-window handler words and seventeen setter cells. (Verified: abi-4's hazard is lowered to low, because both sides of the frame already cross-reference each other and T1 already names the re-proof. abi-11's setter counts depend on how they are counted. Several of the doc mismatches were already listed in ABI-BREAK-LIST section 11, and three duplicate fixes owned by the sched, drivers and loader areas are left to them.)

strengths.title: Direct far calls into a fixed table, no fixups
strengths.why: No relocation and no load-time patching, and a call costs one far call. DOS paid an int dispatch, Mac a trap exception, Win16 a fixup chain plus entry-table thunks. This is the right model for a 4.77 MHz 8088.

strengths.title: Cell shape follows heat, and inline cells are measured
strengths.why: Calls made every frame stay fast while rare calls cost 6 bytes. OSAPI_ICELL/IEND make a length mismatch an assembly error on whichever build has it.

strengths.title: The ABI is checked in the binary
strengths.why: t_api_abi decodes kernel.bin by cell length, resolves each target in the section its shape names, and its ALIAS/INLINE/FIXED ledgers cannot go stale in either direction.

strengths.title: The lock turns a version bump into a decision
strengths.why: 258 recorded decisions and 5 bumps. Contract comments are part of the fingerprint, and LD_EVER gives the user a refusal message they can act on.

strengths.title: The dispatcher at +12 plus one wm_pkgcall site
strengths.why: Every callback is an ordinary near proc, re-entrant across packages, with DS taken from W_SEG and ES = KERNEL_SEG. A package author cannot forget a retf. This beats Win16's MakeProcInstance and exported prologs.

strengths.title: Marshalling happens in one layer
strengths.why: X cells hand the caller's DS over in ES. N cells copy names into a 13-byte buffer with a forced NUL, so a hostile name cannot run on.

strengths.title: One SDK and one table, refusals rather than holes
strengths.why: A cell kern_small lacks answers CF=1 instead of disappearing. This is OS/2's Family API idea without a bind step.

strengths.title: Branch on the capabilities, never on the CPU tier
strengths.why: OSAPI_XMEM_CAPS, SND_CAPS and FSX_CAPS answer what is actually present. That is Gestalt's lesson, learned without Gestalt.

strengths.title: Tables versioned by their own length byte
strengths.why: DRV_H_DSV and DRV_H_FSV record how long a driver's service tables were when it was built, and the kernel zero-fills the rest: RegisterClassEx's cbSize in one byte each. It is the pattern for snapshot buffers (R2) and the window-class rethink.

strengths.title: Cells double as module doors (apic_*)
strengths.why: A module far-calls the public cell instead of growing a private shim, and the label follows the cell through any renumber.

strengths.title: t_mirror maintains itself
strengths.why: Any constant defined in more than one file is compared, so a newly mirrored constant is covered the day it appears.

findings.title: OSAPI_RAND's low bits repeat with a short period, and six games read them
findings.detail: osapi_rand computes seed = seed*25173 + 13849 mod 2^16 and returns the seed. 25173 is 1 mod 4 and the increment is odd, so bit 0 alternates on every call, bits 0-1 have period 4 and bits 0-2 period 8. From any seed, x&3 cycles 3,0,1,2. Tank, DotDel, Tamegram, WireBall and Pixelstein all mask the low bits; Tank's `test al,1` is a strict alternation, not a coin. The seed is also one system-wide word, so one package's SRAND re-seeds every other package and two games interleave each other's streams. The SDK says neither.
evidence: apps/os88api.inc:348-349 (SRAND/RAND contract says nothing about the shared seed)
findings.recommendation: Add `xchg ah, al` after the store, so AL carries bits 8-15 (period of at least 512) and the stored seed is unchanged. Update SPEC.md 20.4's 'out AX = seed'. Document that the seed is shared and that a package needing a reproducible stream carries its own LCG (~14 bytes). Re-baseline any test that asserts a seeded sequence.
findings.prior_art: DOS and Win16 C runtimes keep the seed per process; ANSI C rand() implementations return the high bits for this reason.
findings.verify_note: Re-read kernel.asm:6599-6607: one shared word [osapi_seed], seed*25173+13849 returned whole. 25173 = 1 mod 4 and the increment is odd, so bit 0 alternates and the low k bits have period 2^k. Read all six sites: Tank's second draw (`test al,1`) is fixed by the first draw's parity, Tamegram's three draws per spawn (and 7 / and 1 / and 3) walk a period-8 pattern. `xchg ah, al` is 86 E0, two bytes: +2 holds. Not in ABI-BREAK-LIST or KERNEL-BYTE-QUEUE.

findings.title: kern_small's OSAPI_FS_OP overwrites AX although the contract says every register is kept
findings.detail: kern_small has no FPG_PARK, so cell 0x04EF there is OSAPI_XREFUSE (mov ax,1 / cmp al,2 / retf). The SDK contract lists kern_small among the refusals and ends 'Every register kept'. kern_big's body does keep AX. Callers state the contract they rely on. None read AX afterwards today, so this is latent. OSAPI_VOL_CHECK uses the same refusal and its contract does say '(AX = 1)'.
findings.recommendation: Make the SDK say 'kern_small: CF=1, AX=1 (OSAPI_XREFUSE)', copying VOL_CHECK's wording, and run abilock --update without a bump. Alternatively make the cell stc/retf plus four NOPs (still six bytes) and add a FIXED row to t_api_abi.
findings.verify_note: FPG_PARK is defined only under KERN_BIG (kernel.asm:1303-1307), so on kern_small cell 0x04EF is OSAPI_XREFUSE = mov ax,1 / cmp al,2 / retf (kernel.asm:2601-2605, 4430-4439). The SDK ends 'Every register kept' (os88api.inc:2565) while VOL_CHECK's says '(AX = 1)'. dsl_opgo and os88partsbody read only CF and flags, so the bug is latent. kern_emu and kern_mega define KERN_BIG, so only kern_small is affected.

findings.title: t_api_abi decodes only kern_big's table
findings.detail: The gate opens build/kernel.bin and nothing else. Thirteen %if arms inside the table produce kern_small, kern_emu and kern_mega shapes that are never decoded. Only the per-cell ICELL length check and one total-length assert hold them, and the total cannot see two length changes that cancel out in different arms. The FIXED ledger has no rows for kern_small's two XREFUSE cells, so the gate would fail there today, which shows it has never been run there. The invariant that matters is that all four kernels' cells start at the same offsets, and that can be checked from the four symbol maps.
findings.recommendation: Add a --kernel mode for build/smallk, emuk and megak with per-kernel FIXED rows; kern_mega's SLOT `1E E8 .. .. 1F CB 90 90` and its ICW jump cells need decoders. Add a cross-kernel comparison of cell start offsets. Register it where those kernels are built (full tier).
findings.verify_note: main() opens only build/kernel.bin (t_api_abi.py:458, not 443). FIXED (lines 303-307) has no FS_OP or VOL_CHECK rows, and the FIXED branch (lines 527-532) fails a name it has no row for, so kern_small's XREFUSE cell at 0x04EF would fail. Registered once, fast tier (suite.py:847).

findings.title: An N-cell body reads the caller's DS out of api_rn's stack frame at a literal offset
findings.detail: dwsf_dskw_write_seq applies WSQF_SYS's driver check to `mov bx,[bp+10]`. That word is the caller's DS that api_rn pushed under api_far's far frame, and the offset is counted by hand in a comment with nothing asserting it. T1 (five-byte rare cells) reshapes exactly this frame. If the offset shifts, the check judges the caller's SI or BP as its segment, granting or refusing system-file appends on a wrong value.
evidence: docs/plans/ABI-BREAK-LIST.md T1 ('the stack shape of the X/N bodies must be re-proved')
findings.recommendation: Define API_RN_DSOFF equ 10 beside api_rn with the push sequence and use it in diskw.inc. Name this reader in T1's row.
findings.listed_as: T1 (new evidence: a hidden reader of the frame T1 changes)
findings.verify_note: The offset is right today. dwsf's push bx / push bp sits over api_far's popped frame, so the stack reads IP, CS, SI, DS, giving [bp+10] = the caller's DS (diskw.inc:3397-3414, kernel.asm:4747-4767). Nothing asserts it, but each side's comment names the other: api_rn says 'dwsf_dskw_write_seq reads the DS there', and dwsf spells the frame out. ABI-BREAK-LIST T1 already says 'the stack shape of the X/N bodies must be re-proved'. Severity lowered to low: the hazard fires only inside T1, which already names the re-proof.

findings.title: OSAPI_DRV_CALL promises DI back, but neither the kernel nor the driver contract keeps it
findings.detail: The SDK says DI reaches the driver as set 'and comes back yours'. drv_pkg_call_x pops the caller's DI before the far call and restores only BP and DS after it. The driver-side contract says 'out whatever you define', so the promise holds only if every verb of every driver preserves DI. Also, 'CF=1 AX=0 = no driver' cannot be told apart from a driver verb refusing with AX=0.
findings.recommendation: Make the driver contract say 'preserve DI; BP is spent'. A kernel push/pop of DI around the call is +2 bytes and +2 stack on ETHER's 272/384-byte service-worker chain, so the doc fix is the right one.
findings.verify_note: drv_pkg_call_x pops the caller's DI before the far call and restores only BP and DS after it (driver.inc:6614-6662). The SDK says DI 'comes back yours' (os88api.inc:3456-3460). The driver contract says 'out whatever you define' (os88drv.inc:377). On the no-driver path (.none) AX = 0 with CF = 1, which cannot be told apart from a verb refusing with AX = 0.

findings.title: No runtime API level: a package cannot ask which cells this kernel has
findings.detail: PKG_FMT is an equality test, a MAJOR number. Since format 10 the table has only grown, so the table's end works as a MINOR number, and The Wire already reasons in it (WIRE_CELL_LEVELS, WIRE_TABLE_END). The guest cannot. SPEC.md 20.2.0.1's 'What it does not cover' is exactly a new package far-calling past an old table. Bytes 0060:0006-0007 are padding today.
findings.recommendation: NOW: put `dw osapi_table_end` at 0060:0006 (replaces padding). Add an SDK macro OS88_NEED cell for the entry proc (cmp word [es:6], cell+1 / jb refuse); an old kernel reads 0 and refuses. Have os88pkg.py warn when a package calls past the last released level without it. FLAG DAY: carry the needed level in the header and have ld_hdr_ok answer LD_EVER when it exceeds osapi_table_end. First confirm that no PKG_FMT-10 kernel predates SPEC.md 57's registry, which moved a mouse-instrument word off 0060:0006.
findings.bytes_est: 0 resident now (padding); ~+8 .cold loader at the flag day; ~10 bytes per opting package
findings.prior_art: GEOS geode protocol numbers (major must match, minor >=), AmigaOS OpenLibrary(name, version), Win16 load-time import resolution ('Call to Undefined Dynalink'), DOS int 21h AH=30h.
findings.verify_note: Bytes 0x06-0x07 are `times` padding today (kernel.asm:2346-2360). ld_hdr_ok is an equality test (loader.inc:292-300). SPEC.md 20.2.0.1's 'What it does not cover' (44213) names exactly this gap and leaves only The Wire to fence it. Caveat for the macro: before SPEC.md 57's registry a mouse-instrument word lived at 0060:0006 (SPEC.md 14071), so a kernel that old may not read 0 there. Check that every PKG_FMT-10 kernel post-dates 57 before relying on 'an old kernel reads 0'.

findings.title: Packages write the window record's geometry, which the SDK says they may not
findings.detail: The SDK says the fields are 'readable by contract, not writable'. Paint's pt_wfix writes W_W/W_H/W_X/W_Y from a size-changed callback. The Sticky library hides the window, writes the fields, then shows it. The kernel keeps derived state these writes bypass (W_NATR, W_ZOOMR, W_SUEXT). The writes exist because no door sets geometry without repainting: OSAPI_WM_RESIZE always repaints and cannot be used from the callback Paint is in.
findings.recommendation: Add a no-repaint/hidden mode to OSAPI_WM_RESIZE (top bit of CX), or legalise hide-write-show for HIDDEN windows only. Add a host lint for stores to [es:..+W_*] under apps/ with an allow-list.
findings.prior_art: Win16 SetWindowPos SWP_NOREDRAW/SWP_NOMOVE; Mac SizeWindow(fUpdate=false). The Mac exposed WindowRecord and Carbon had to retrofit accessors.
findings.verify_note: pt_wfix writes W_W, W_H, W_X and W_Y through ES = KERNEL_SEG (paint.asm:12831-12870). os88stik.inc writes W_Y (1023, 1712) and W_W/W_H/W_X/W_Y (2376-2407). The SDK at os88api.inc:3170-3174 says 'readable by contract, not writable'. W_NATR, W_ZOOMR and W_SUEXT are W_SIDE+16..+32 (wm.inc:117-119).

findings.title: Rules about which task or context may call a cell are prose, and SPEC admits one has no enforcement
findings.detail: Each cell's context lives in its comment: UI task only, any, worker-safe, bracket-only, lock held, FSXF_RATE-hook-safe. SPEC.md 20.3 calls the file slots' UI-task rule 'an author rule with no enforcement behind it'. What it protects is global state: the single api_name/api_name2 staging buffer and [api_sysfp], which is written through CS. No file cell tests [sch_cur].
evidence: SPEC.md 20.3 'The file slots are UI-task/window-callback context only'
findings.recommendation: Put a machine-readable tag (; @ctx ui|any|worker|hook|lock) in each contract comment, where abilock already fingerprints it. Add a host gate on stkdepth's call graph: no worker root (OSAPI_TASK_SPAWN target, OSAPI_DRV_TASK) and no FSXF_RATE hook may reach a cell its tag forbids. Have docs/INDEX.md print the tag.
findings.prior_art: Inside Macintosh's per-routine 'may move or purge memory' and interrupt-safety tables.
findings.verify_note: SPEC.md:44973 says 'an author rule with no enforcement behind it'. api_name and api_name2 are single shared .text buffers (kernel.asm:5213-5214), and [api_sysfp] is written through CS (kernel.asm:5007-5011).

findings.title: CF is the only common sign of a refusal
findings.detail: On CF=1 from an absent capability, AX is 0 (DRV_CALL with no driver), 1 (XREFUSE, FERR_NODISK, FSKE_NOTHERE), FERR_PROT (kern_small's system-file stubs), untouched (every stc/ret stub, and kern_mega's real-mode bracket filling the table with stc), or a family code (7 for an unknown sound verb, DRVE_*).
findings.recommendation: NOW: state in the SDK preamble that CF=1 is the only universal refusal and that AX carries meaning only where a cell names a code family. FLAG DAY: adopt AX=1 = 'no such service/verb on this kernel' everywhere. XREFUSE, FERR_NODISK and FSKE_NOTHERE already answer 1; DRV_CALL's 0 and the stubs that leave AX untouched move, most by sharing XREFUSE.
findings.bytes_est: ~0 (stubs that keep their own body +3 each)
findings.prior_art: DOS: CF + AX, error 1 = invalid function. Mac: one OSErr space for the whole system.
findings.verify_note: Checked four of the codes. DRV_CALL's .none answers AX=0 (driver.inc:6655-6659), XREFUSE AX=1, kern_small's system-file cells AX=FERR_PROT (kernel.asm:5000-5004), and kern_mega's real-mode bracket fills the table with stc (fsx.inc:2341-2351), leaving AX untouched.

findings.title: Contracts are written in up to four places, and the copies have gone stale
findings.detail: The SDK %define comments are the fingerprinted authority. SPEC.md 20.3's slot-contract block is a second copy, stale in at least four entries (SND_PLAY, SND_CAPS, FSX_RUN, FSX_WAIT). SPEC.md 53.8 is a third with the same omissions. kernel.asm's table comments are a fourth, often a dozen lines per cell. SPEC.md already refuses to keep a second copy of the address map for this exact reason.
findings.recommendation: Delete SPEC.md 20.3's contract block and 53.8's, pointing at the SDK names. Cut each kernel cell comment to one line naming the SDK symbol and the §. Drop SPEC.md 20.3's running cell-count paragraph, which says itself it is not a contract.
findings.verify_note: SPEC.md 20.3's block is stale for SND_CAPS (44804), SND_PLAY (44811-44816), FSX_CAPS (44908), FSX_RUN (44910-44912) and FSX_WAIT (44921). 53.8 is stale the same way (107740-107751); the video area's fix covers 53.8. ABI-BREAK-LIST 11 already lists SND_PLAY and kernel.asm's stale 'keeps its NUMBER' block. The doc_fixes below repair the 20.3 entries now; deleting the copies is the recommendation.

findings.title: The window record holds ten handler words that belong in a per-class table in the package
findings.detail: Each window record holds ten near pointers into the package's own segment (W_ONSIZE/ONMOUSEUP/ONDRAG/ONTIMER, W_ONSZ/ONWK/ONCL/ONRC/ABOUT/ONWH). They are stored per window in kernel .bss (WIN_SIZE 74 x MAX_WIN 12) and each is installed by its own cell: 219 setter call sites. Seven flag setters add 128 more sites. The wm_create template is a fixed 8 words, which is why every later handler became a cell. Rethink: one W_CLASS word pointing at a table in the package segment: a length byte (the DSV pattern), a style word (the seven flags), then the handler offsets. wm_pkgcall reads it with DS already the package's. Kernel windows share const tables. The table moves with the package under compaction for free. The cost is ~20 cycles per callback.
evidence: setter census (method-dependent): asm `call` sites alone ONTIMER 29, ONWAKE 31, SNAP 30; every mention ONTIMER 48, ONWAKE 59, SNAP 72
findings.recommendation: At the flag day, price this against K17-2/K17-3: it removes the setters and the record words together, and the template's fixed shape with them.
findings.bytes_est: ~-200 to -260 resident kern_big (-216 .bss record, -60..-110 table, +~80 dispatch and kernel class tables); ~-1.5KB unpacked across packages
findings.prior_art: Win16 WNDCLASS (window procedure per class) and WS_* styles at CreateWindow; Mac window definition procs.
findings.verify_note: Ten handler words confirmed (wm.inc:45-121), and the template is a fixed 8 words (os88api.inc WT_*). The setter census is method-dependent. Counting `call OSAPI_WM_<X>` in asm alone gives ONTIMER 29, ONWAKE 31 and SNAP 30, against the reviewer's 41/36/51. Counting every non-%define mention gives 48/59/72. Read the figures as order-of-magnitude. The byte estimate is unchanged: 9 words x 12 windows = -216 .bss holds.

findings.title: Multiplexed doors take their verb in AL, AH or BL
findings.detail: AL: SND_FM/STREAM/PLAY, FSX_SPK, FILE_COPY, VOL_CHECK, WM_DESK, DSK_CACHE, SERIAL, THM_SET. AH: MEM_COMPACT, DRV_USE. BL: OSAPI_SEG, OSAPI_MEM_P, OSAPI_DRV_CALL (BH = class). Each had a local reason, but a reader cannot guess which.
evidence: apps/os88api.inc OSAPI_MEM_COMPACT, OSAPI_DRV_USE, OSAPI_SEG, OSAPI_MEM_P, OSAPI_DRV_CALL contracts
findings.recommendation: NOW: a rule for the next door (verb in AL unless AL is an argument, then BL). FLAG DAY: move the AH outliers only where another row already reopens the cell.
findings.prior_art: DOS int 21h: AH = function, AL = subfunction, unchanged from 1981.
findings.verify_note: Spot-checked: OSAPI_MEM_COMPACT takes AH = MEMC_* (os88api.inc:1736) and OSAPI_DRV_USE AL = class with AH = verb (7059-7061).

findings.title: Names collide across subsystems
findings.detail: CLIP means both the clipboard (CLIP_PUT/GET/SIZE) and the clip region (WM_CLIP_*). FS means both a DRVC_FILE listing (FS_ENT) and the progress widget (FS_PROG/FS_OP). DESK means a desktop item, the desk layer and the theme ground. Several names break the SUBSYS_VERB shape: GET_TICKS, SET_COLOR, FULLSCREEN, DECOMP, TOAST, REBOOT, SERIAL, SEG, BATCH_*, ABOUT_SET.
findings.recommendation: Adopt a naming rule for new cells now. Renames are source-only (no cell moves, a fingerprint update, no bump): do them at the flag day with one cycle of %define aliases.

findings.title: 'ES:SI' in an X cell's contract actually means DS:SI
findings.detail: OSAPI_GFX_SPANS documents 'ES:SI', but api_x overwrites ES with the caller's DS. SLOT cells such as GFX_BLIT4, FILE_READ (ES:BX) and XMEM_COPY read a real caller-chosen ES. That is three conventions under two spellings.
findings.recommendation: Write X-cell pointer arguments as 'SI (in your DS; ES is not read)', so the register named is the register read.
findings.verify_note: Real but milder than stated. OSAPI_GFX_SPANS' own contract continues 'ES is yours - the stub puts your DS there - so the list lives in your own segment' (os88api.inc:1952-1955), so the reader is told. The defect is only that the register named is not the register read.

findings.title: No parameter validation, and no build option that adds it
findings.detail: Window arguments are trusted everywhere. The inline setters store through [cs:bx+W_*] and wm_sizable ORs into [bx+W_FLAGS], so a bad BX writes anywhere in KERNEL_SEG. That fits SPEC.md 20.8's trust model, but Windows 3.1's retail parameter validation and its debug kernel are what found most Win16 misuse.
findings.recommendation: Add an APICHK=1 knob (0 shipped bytes). Window-taking cells become same-length padded jump cells into a validating stub (BX in the window table, W_SEG = the caller's DS); file cells check [sch_cur]=0. One soak row runs the package sweep on that kernel.
findings.prior_art: Windows 3.1 parameter validation and debug KERNEL RIPs.
findings.verify_note: Spot-checked: wm_sizable ORs into [bx+W_FLAGS] with no check (wm.inc:4277-4284), and the inline setters store through [cs:bx+W_*] (kernel.asm:2824).

findings.title: The package header has no room left to grow
findings.detail: All eight bits of the flags byte at +3 are defined. +4 is already overloaded as the packed length when the package has parts. +15's class has six bits but only five classes, and an index past SCH_NCLASS is refused as hostile, so those bits cannot be reused without old kernels refusing. Every optional block costs a flag bit.
findings.recommendation: At the flag day, reserve one bit for 'an extension list follows the clear prefix' (type, length, data) so future blocks, starting with abi-6's needed level, take no bit.
findings.prior_art: NE/PE headers reaching variable tables from a fixed header; Mac typed resources.
findings.verify_note: SPEC.md 20.2's flags row defines bits 0-7: icon, assoc, parts, compressed, LZ format, glyph, desk, stik. SCH_NCLASS is 5 in a 6-bit field, refused past the end (sched.inc:2872-2881).

findings.title: Every cell preserves every register, and C packages throw that work away
findings.detail: The contract is 'every register except documented outputs', so each kernel body saves what it touches. The C SDK treats AX, BX, CX, DX, SI, DI, ES and FLAGS as clobbered, so for every C package that saving is pure cost. Win16 and OS/2 1.x treated AX/BX/CX/DX/ES as volatile.
findings.recommendation: New argument for V1: C callers already treat everything as clobbered. A surface-wide switch would break hand-written asm silently, so keep it limited to V1's rect primitives.
findings.prior_art: Win16/OS/2 Pascal convention: AX-DX and ES volatile; SI, DI, BP, DS preserved.
findings.verify_note: os88thunk.asm:62-66: 'AX, BX, CX, DX, SI, DI, ES and FLAGS are all fair game and the compiler expects them to be gone'. Already argued under V1.

doc_fixes.old_text: ; Packages run in the kernel's near model: CS = DS = KERNEL_SEG, but
doc_fixes.new_text:
; Packages run in their OWN segment: CS = DS = the region the loader gave
; them (SPEC.md 20.1), but
doc_fixes.why: The same header says at line 39 and line 55 that a package owns a segment with CS = DS = it; wm.inc:446 loads DS from W_SEG for every callback.

doc_fixes.old_text: ; It is baked into every OSAPI_* far call, so a
doc_fixes.new_text: ; KERNEL_SEG (above) is baked into every OSAPI_* far call, so a
doc_fixes.why: These lines sit under VT_FILE's comment but are about KERNEL_SEG (defined at line 74), the only value 'baked into every OSAPI_* far call'.

doc_fixes.old_text: ; Each slot is an 8-byte cell at 0x0010 + 8n, and `call OSAPI_*` is a FAR
doc_fixes.new_text:
; The cells are packed from 0x0010 in several lengths (SPEC.md 20.3), so an
; address is the sum of the cells before it; `call OSAPI_*` is a FAR
doc_fixes.why: kernel.asm:4493 asserts the table as 44 cells of 8, 11 of 7, 119 of 6, 6 of 3, ... (1,259 bytes); kernel.asm:2406 says 'The offsets are therefore NOT 0x0010 + 8n'.

doc_fixes.old_text: ; preserved, flags included.
doc_fixes.new_text:
; preserved. FLAGS are not, unless a cell's own contract says so - CF is the
; commonest answer.
doc_fixes.why: Most cells answer in CF, CLC_OR_STC tails (kernel.asm:2608-2623) also write ZF/SF/PF/OF, and gfx_hline documents 'clobbers: flags' (vga12.inc:1064); only a few contracts (MENU_SET, inst_pkg_alive) promise the FLAGS word.

doc_fixes.old_text: ; --- window record layout (SPEC.md 11, 20 bytes) -------------------------------
doc_fixes.new_text: ; --- window record layout (SPEC.md 11): 34 published bytes on kern_big, 28 on kern_small
doc_fixes.why: The published words below run to W_TIMER (+32, a word) on kern_big and stop at W_ONMOUSEUP (+26) on kern_small (wm.inc:45-104); WIN_SIZE is 74 / 65 (wm.inc:127, 132).

doc_fixes.old_text:
; THE LAST THREE WORDS ARE kern_big's ALONE. The 128KB kernel's record STOPS
; at 28 bytes (SPEC.md 13.8.2), so on that machine offset 28 is the NEXT
; window's W_FLAGS and offset 32 is its W_W - naming any of the three there
